source.title: Improving Transformer Performance for French Clinical Notes Classification Using Mixture of Experts on a Limited Dataset
source.authors: Thanh-Dung Le; P. Jouvet; R. Noumeir

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text includes the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training and validation performance on natural clinical labels and explicitly describes a generalization gap, using a different setting and measurement from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a training-validation gap, but does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, CNN versus fully connected architectures, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Hyperparameter choices are not separate result rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports clinical classification performance and uses dropout and small-batch training motivated by generalization considerations. Its own results test none of V1–V8: a training–validation gap alone does not establish any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the gap discussion, but only part of the conclusion. The authors conclude that their small MoE-Transformer offers competitive clinical classification performance with substantially shorter training than the biomedical pretrained comparators. They also report limitations in clinical contextual understanding and attribute the remaining generalization gap to insufficient data and sharp minima; that sharpness attribution is not established by a perturbation measurement.
record.recipe_differences: A French clinical-note classification experiment with a MoE-Transformer trained from scratch; no version-specific intervention or measurement is reproduced.
record.method_sensitivity: Training duration: the authors describe overfitting after epoch 30 and a later decrease in loss during the 500-epoch run without early stopping.

fits_no_version.finding: At epoch 30, the MoE-Transformer achieved 98% training accuracy and 87% validation accuracy on French clinical narratives.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High training accuracy can coexist with an 11-percentage-point training–validation gap on a limited clinical text dataset.

record.code_released: not stated; data and reproducible codes are available upon request from Prof. Philippe Jouvet.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Journal of Translational Engineering in Health and Medicine
record.problems: The reported generalization-gap result is for one clinical text dataset and one MoE-Transformer setting; no uncertainty estimate is stated. The paper's sharp-minimum characterization is not supported by a magnitude-aware perturbation comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results were reported for the listed versions. The paper's comparisons of classifiers and training times do not test those versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out random-label accuracy, compared with natural-label performance under the same recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error. The reported descent over epochs is not a width sweep.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning. Adam and AdamW are used in different model recipes without an optimizer ablation.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes. Batch-size tuning is described without comparative results.
The effect of adding, removing, or varying dropout under otherwise comparable conditions.

Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps across networks, and its ranking against other measures. Learning curves and embedding visualizations do not measure this.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. References to large-batch generalization, dropout, and double descent do not substitute for the required comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label evaluation.
No width sweep or comparison beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
Does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or compare it with other generalization measures. The paper's sharp-minimum discussion does not test the version's stated relation.
No removal of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: MoE-Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared training and validation classification accuracy at the 30th epoch.
rows.note: The paper describes a training-validation generalization gap; this is a clinical text classification setting, not one of the listed version-specific tests.
rows.check: The reported 98% training and 87% validation accuracies at epoch 30 match Section IV. They measure a generalization gap but cannot establish any listed version; the row's observed state should not imply otherwise.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
